sources.entry: macOrganizer - macOS app for organizing files or removing unnecessary files.

summary.one_liner: macOrganizer is a macOS (OS X) app that sorts files in a chosen folder into organized groups or removes unnecessary files such as duplicates and archives.
summary.what_it_does: The app lets you pick either an organize mode or a cleanup mode, then choose a folder to act on. In cleanup mode it targets duplicate and archive files. Removed files are moved to the Trash rather than deleted permanently, so you can review them before they are gone. The README describes the workflow as a simple GUI: select mode, choose folder, then press the organize or delete button. It does not document the exact sorting rules or how duplicates are detected.
use_cases: organize a cluttered downloads folder on mac
clean up archive files on macOS
free up disk space by reviewing trashed duplicates
how_to_run: Download the latest version (1.0) from the repository releases
Select organize or remove unnecessary files
Press the choose folder button and select a folder
Press the organize or delete button to perform the action
notable: Cleanup moves duplicates and archives to the Trash instead of deleting them permanently
Two modes: organize files or remove unnecessary files
Simple folder-based workflow with no setup required beyond unzipping the app
caveats: README does not describe how files are organized or how duplicates are identified
Only version 1.0 is referenced in the README; maintenance status is not stated
